blurb: The space programme, the missions and the vehicles, written for a paper that asks which year and which rocket rather than how the physics works.

topics.title: ISRO: the missions, the launch vehicles and the people
topics.hook: Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to land near the lunar south pole, and the fourth to soft-land at all. The rest of the programme is a list worth memorising.
topics.story:
**ISRO** was formed on **15 August 1969**, succeeding INCOSPAR which **Vikram Sarabhai** had set up in 1962. Sarabhai is called the father of the Indian space programme; the first sounding rocket flew from **Thumba** in Kerala in 1963. Headquarters are in **Bengaluru**; the main launch site is the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota**, Andhra Pradesh. The current chairman is **V. Narayanan**, who took over in January 2025 from S. Somanath.

**Satellites and firsts.** **Aryabhata**, India's first satellite, launched by the Soviet Union in 1975. **Rohini RS-1**, 1980, the first launched by an Indian vehicle, the SLV-3, under **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam** as project director. **INSAT** for communications, **IRS** for remote sensing, **NavIC** for regional navigation.

**Launch vehicles.** **PSLV**, the workhorse, which in February 2017 launched **104 satellites** in a single flight, a record at the time. **GSLV**, which uses a cryogenic upper stage, indigenous from 2014. **LVM3**, formerly GSLV Mk III, the heaviest, which launched Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 and is planned for Gaganyaan. **SSLV**, for small satellites, first successful flight 2023.

**Planetary missions.** **Chandrayaan-1 (2008)** confirmed water molecules on the Moon through the Moon Impact Probe and NASA's M3 instrument. **Mangalyaan**, the Mars Orbiter Mission, launched 5 November 2013 and inserted into Mars orbit on **24 September 2014**, made India the first country to reach Mars on its first attempt, and the cheapest such mission at about ₹450 crore. **Chandrayaan-2 (2019)** lost the Vikram lander but its orbiter still works. **Chandrayaan-3** landed on **23 August 2023** near the lunar south pole, with the **Vikram** lander and **Pragyan** rover; the date is now observed as **National Space Day**. **Aditya-L1**, launched 2 September 2023, reached the L1 Lagrange point in January 2024 to study the Sun.

**Gaganyaan** is the crewed programme, with four Indian Air Force test pilots announced as astronaut-designates in February 2024, one of whom, Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, flew to the International Space Station on a commercial mission in 2025.

timeline.what: INCOSPAR set up under Vikram Sarabhai

topics.why: Space passages are common and the questions are factual: which vehicle, which year, which landing site. Chandrayaan-3 and the south pole is the single most likely question.

nodes.label: Vikram Sarabhai
nodes.note: Set up INCOSPAR in 1962 and founded the Physical Research Laboratory at Ahmedabad in 1947. Died in 1971.

nodes.label: Chandrayaan-3 (2023)
nodes.note: Landed 23 August 2023 near the lunar south pole. Vikram lander, Pragyan rover. India became the fourth country to soft-land.

nodes.label: Mars Orbiter Mission
nodes.note: Launched 5 November 2013, Mars orbit 24 September 2014. First country to succeed on its first attempt.

nodes.label: PSLV
nodes.note: Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle. Launched 104 satellites on a single flight in February 2017.

nodes.label: Satish Dhawan Space Centre
nodes.note: At Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. Named after ISRO’s second chairman.

nodes.label: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
nodes.note: Project director for SLV-3, which put Rohini in orbit in 1980. Later President of India, 2002 to 2007.

nodes.label: Chandrayaan-1 (2008)
nodes.note: Its Moon Impact Probe and NASA’s M3 instrument confirmed water molecules on the lunar surface.

nodes.label: Chandrayaan-2 (2019)
nodes.note: The Vikram lander crashed but the orbiter continues to function and relayed data for Chandrayaan-3.

nodes.label: Aditya-L1
nodes.note: Launched 2 September 2023, reached the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange point in January 2024.

nodes.label: LVM3
nodes.note: Formerly GSLV Mk III. Launched Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 and is planned for Gaganyaan.

nodes.label: Gaganyaan
nodes.note: Four Indian Air Force test pilots named as astronaut-designates in February 2024.

nodes.label: NavIC
nodes.note: Indian regional navigation satellite system, formerly IRNSS. Covers India and 1,500 km around it.

nodes.label: GSLV
nodes.note: Uses a cryogenic upper stage, indigenous from the January 2014 flight after the technology was denied under MTCR pressure in the 1990s.

nodes.label: Thumba
nodes.note: Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station in Kerala, from which the first sounding rocket flew in 1963.

nodes.label: National Space Day
nodes.note: Declared after the Chandrayaan-3 landing; the landing site is named Shiv Shakti Point.
